narrative.overview: A developer's front door that reads like a bench of finished work: who he is in one line, a way to reach him in one click, then the live projects laid out side by side. The page borrows GitHub's typography, canvas, and light/dark behavior and spends its expressive budget on the brand-colored contact badges, the two-column project cards, and the coding illustration.
keyCharacteristics: Brand-colored, square-cornered contact badges as the primary call to action.
Projects as a 2×2 card grid with live links, never a bare list.
Every data image paired light/dark through <picture>.
Calm, professional copy; one line of personality.

rules.name: The Accents-Stay-Up-Top Rule
rules.body: Saturated brand color appears only in the contact badge row.

rules.name: The Paired-Image Rule
rules.body: Any image that contains a background or text color ships as a <picture> with a prefers-color-scheme: dark source.

rules.name: The One-H1 Rule
rules.body: The name is the only <h1>. Headings never skip a level.

dos: Do lead with shipped, live projects; every card has a working link.
Do pair every colored data image with a dark variant via <picture>.
Do keep brand color in the contact badges.
Do write alt text that carries the same information as the image.
donts: Don't neutralize the contact badges to gray or replace the project cards with a plain Markdown table.
Don't add badge walls, typing-SVG banners, or trophy grids.
Don't invent metrics, employers, or years of experience.
Don't rely on anything GitHub strips: style, class, script, custom fonts.
